cutoffRationale: Every source is pinned to its last revision before this date. ChatGPT shipped 2022-11-30 and the model-written web grew from there, so a corpus scraped at HEAD is partly machine-written. Measuring a false-positive rate against contaminated text flatters the linter: generated prose in the negative set makes real tells look like acceptable human variation.

sources.why: The closest register to what AntiSlop is pointed at: careful human technical prose, edited, book-length, with code interleaved. The strongest test of the skip mask.
Committee-written docs prose. Heavy on the arrow, pipeline, and breadcrumb conventions the arrow rule exempts, so it is where a bad exemption shows up first.
Many authors, many hands, lightly edited. Closer to the variance of real published writing than a single-voice book.

Pinned to pre-cutoff revision ids through the MediaWiki API, which is an exact pre-LLM Wikipedia rather than an approximate one: the API resolves the last revision before the cutoff and fetches that id, so later edits cannot leak in. Half technical and half not, because a rule that only ever sees software prose is not calibrated.

A deliberate control rather than a target. Definitely human and definitely not generated, so any rule that fires heavily here is matching English rather than machine authorship. Expect the em-dash rate to be high: that is a fact about Victorian typography, and it is the reason em-dash defaults off rather than evidence the rule is broken.

Human and generated intros for the SAME Wikipedia article. Pairing controls for topic, which unpaired corpora cannot: a rate difference here is the rule responding to how the text was written rather than to what it is about. Pairs directly against the wikipedia source above.
Human and ChatGPT answers to the same question. The explanatory register is the closest public paired data to the blog and guide writing this linter is pointed at.

sources.register: student essays, Reuters news, creative writing
sources.why: The benchmark from Ghostbuster (NAACL 2024), hosted as plain text files on GitHub, so it uses the same pinned-SHA fetch path as the human sources rather than a second hosting dependency. Human sides are IvyPanda essays, the Reuters 50-50 authorship set, and the top r/WritingPrompts posters collected October 2022, which is before ChatGPT was public. Paired by prompt across variants. The paper describes five prompting strategies; the release does not document which folder is which, so gpt_prompt1 is labeled only as an alternate prompting strategy.

slopCaveats: Vintage. The generators are GPT-3 curie, ChatGPT 3.5, and Claude, all 2022 and 2023. Current models write differently, and several tells in this linter postdate these datasets. Recall measured here is a FLOOR.

Register. Encyclopedic intros, Q&A answers, student essays, news, and creative writing, rather than the landing copy, launch posts, and newsletters where slop is thickest and where this linter is actually pointed. Marketing prose would score higher.

Prompting. These were generated by plain completion prompts, not by someone asking for an engaging blog post, so the social-post tells (engagement bait, reveal framing, puffery) have little chance to appear.

RAID (liamdugan/raid) was evaluated and rejected as a source: its rows are grouped by adversarial attack, including a zero_width_space perturbation that would corrupt the invisible-unicode measurement, and its filter index was unavailable across repeated attempts.
